A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLEX-Judge framework and retain matching experiments. Their text, tables, figures, and appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite the changed title and pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original multimodal judging experiments, ablations, and molecular best-of-N and preference-optimization results in Sections 3–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds benchmark evaluations, a 32B model experiment, and visual question answering tests.

M1.justification: The curated 1K text-reasoning dataset, format diversification, multimodal-model fine-tuning, and reasoning-based inference remain unchanged. The added model-size experiment uses the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds Multimodal RewardBench and JudgeAnything, extending evaluation to video understanding, joint audiovisual understanding, and additional cross-modal generation judgments such as video-to-audio. Appendix C.5 also adds direct TextVQA and OK-VQA answering tasks, beyond judging other models' responses.

E2.justification: Established comparisons expand substantially: Table 1 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro and both Qwen2.5-Omni-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbones; Table 2's VL-RewardBench comparison adds Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-7B; Table 3 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. New Table 7 also evaluates against LLaMA-3.2-90B-Vision and LLaVA-1.5-13B.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 32B configuration trained with LoRA, JudgeAnything evaluation under its Overall setting with pairwise ties, and direct VQA testing against the base model. Previously stated training budgets, metrics, and bias controls in Appendix B and Table 6 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing 3B/7B scaling analysis gains a 32B result row in v2 Table 9. New Appendix C.5 tests preservation of non-judgment visual abilities using TextVQA and OK-VQA. Existing reasoning, data-curation, inference-scaling, bias, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain three-sample and five-sample judgment averaging in Table 6 and ten random trials for molecular best-of-N selection in Appendix B.4.1. No new seed information, uncertainty-reporting practice, or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark results, baseline scores, the 32B row, and VQA outcomes while retaining matched original scores. New Table 8 reports FLEX-Omni-7B at 55.3 overall on JudgeAnything. In Table 3, added Gemini-2.5-Pro scores 54.46 overall, exceeding the retained FLEX-VL-7B majority-voting result of 49.29 and changing the leading comparator.

T1.justification: The transfer hypothesis and mathematical descriptions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces a formal theoretical development that is added, removed, or revised in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the claims that minimal text-only reasoning supervision enables zero-shot multimodal judging and useful molecular selection and preference optimization. The new title and supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v1 motivates limited text training as protection against catastrophic forgetting. New Appendix C.5 extends the discussion to ordinary VQA abilities and explicitly concludes that multimodal capabilities are preserved without forgetting. The weak-backbone and context-window limitations in Appendix E remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The caption of v2 Table 9 specifies that the added 32B model was trained with LoRA. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training time, prompts, molecular implementation details, and code/data access information are retained; detailed settings for the new experiments remain sparse.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Multimodal RewardBench, JudgeAnything, OK-VQA, and TextVQA. The substantive research positioning in Section 6 and Appendix A remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Think Once, Judge Anywhere' to 'Text-Only Reasoning Unleashes Zero-Shot Multimodal Evaluators.' v2 adds two appendix subsections and benchmark pointers and removes the obsolete footnote excluding video-understanding evaluation. Most existing prose and section ordering are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7, 8, and 11, expands and reorders comparison rows in Tables 1–3, and adds a scaling row in the renumbered Table 9. Existing figures and qualitative illustrations are retained, with local relocation and reflow rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added backbone comparisons, broader multimodal evaluation, and VQA retention check strengthen evidence for the central transfer claim. The gain is tempered by sparse documentation of new experiments and an uncorrected interpretation: Section 3.2 still claims the highest GenAI-Bench overall performance despite new Table 3 reporting Gemini-2.5-Pro at 54.46 versus FLEX-VL-7B with majority voting at 49.29.
